answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a refundable bond before it can trade, and misbehavior slashes that bond. An attacker cloning a thousand sock-puppets must fund a thousand bonds, so the attacker cost climbs in a spiral while honest agents treat the bond like an oasis of trust they can reclaim by behaving well. The umber ledger of slashed bonds stays public, so repeat offenders carry a visible record that markets can price in.
